# Opening up new fronts in the fight against cholesterol

## Authors

- Russell A DeBose-Boyd<sup>1</sup>
- Jay D Horton<sup>2</sup>

### Affiliations

1. Department of Molecular Genetics and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center Dallas United States Russell.Debose-Boyd@utsouthwestern.edu
2. Departments of Internal Medicine and Molecular Genetics University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center Dallas United States Jay.Horton@utsouthwestern.edu

† Corresponding author

## Abstract

An unexpected connection between a secretory protein called PCSK9 and Sec24A, a well known protein-transport protein, could lead to the development of novel treatments for patients with high levels of low-density lipoproteins in their blood.

results.result_reasoning: The connection between PCSK9 and Sec24A (C3, C4) is stated as a finding but no experimental evidence, methodology, or data are provided in the extracted text to evaluate its validity. This appears to be a commentary discussing work done elsewhere, making it impossible to assess the quality of evidence supporting this connection. The background claims (C1, C2, C7, C8) represent established knowledge but do not validate the novel connection itself.

The therapeutic potential of the PCSK9-Sec24A connection (C5) is explicitly speculative ('could lead to') and depends entirely on the validity of Result R1, which itself lacks supporting evidence in the provided text. While the medical context (C6, C9) is established knowledge, no experimental data, mechanistic studies, or preclinical validation are presented to support the claim that this connection will lead to novel LDL treatments. This represents future speculation rather than a supported finding.
